`class BridgeRegistry<T extends IBridge>`<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`UIBridgeRegistry`](/reference/backends/uibridgeregistry/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [BridgeRegistry.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/BridgeRegistry.java)

An ordered set of bridges of one kind, kept sorted by priority, whose highest bridge answers `get()`.

## Description

Every registry of [`BridgeHandler`](/reference/bridges/bridgehandler/) is a `BridgeRegistry`.
Registering and unregistering are synchronized and publish a new read-only list, so reading never locks.

## Creation details

<a id="BridgeRegistry-constructor"></a>

### BridgeRegistry

`BridgeRegistry(String name)` 

Creates an empty registry; the name, such as `"RENDER"`, appears in the exception of `get()` on an empty registry.

## Method details

<a id="BridgeRegistry-method-register"></a>

### register

`void register(T bridge)` 

Registers a bridge with the priority `0`.

`void register(T bridge, int priority)` 

Registers a bridge with a priority: the highest priority comes first.
A bridge that is already registered moves to its new priority, after the other bridges of that priority.

<a id="BridgeRegistry-method-unregister"></a>

### unregister

`void unregister(T bridge)` 

Removes a bridge; does nothing when the bridge is not registered.

<a id="BridgeRegistry-method-registerDefault"></a>

### registerDefault

`void registerDefault(T bridge)` 

Registers a bridge with the lowest priority, `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, only when the registry is empty, so that any bridge registered later comes before it.
Backends use it for their default UI bridge.

<a id="BridgeRegistry-method-get"></a>

### get

`T get()` 

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: No … bridge registered, call BridgeHandler.….register before using JOID

Returns the bridge of highest priority.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` that names the registry when it is empty, which usually means that no backend is registered.

<a id="BridgeRegistry-method-getBridge"></a>

### getBridge

`<B extends T> B getBridge(Class<B> bridgeClass)` 

Returns the bridge of highest priority that is an instance of the class, or `null` when there is none.

<a id="BridgeRegistry-method-find"></a>

### find

`T find(Predicate<T> filter)` 

Returns the bridge of highest priority that the filter accepts, or `null` when the filter accepts none.

<a id="BridgeRegistry-method-getBridgeList"></a>

### getBridgeList

`List<T> getBridgeList()` 

Returns the registered bridges, read-only, from the lowest priority to the highest.
The list is a snapshot: a later registration does not change it.
